rs12740374.verdict: The new run recovered a supported in-vitro binding difference and a supported Hep3B reporter effect. It still did not establish the T-versus-G direction from those extracts, connect the molecular effects to a causal target gene, or complete a disease mechanism.
rs12740374.factor_recovery: CEBPA is implicated by the accepted EMSA/antibody observation; the acting member in endogenous liver remains unresolved.
rs12740374.repair_result: Two source-local repair calls. The first retained E1017 and led to supported C5. The second proposed an unlisted sentence range and was correctly refused; a later normal extraction retained the reporter result as E1018/C10.
notes: T7 read Musunuru et al. (PMID 20686566, PMC3062476). Five literature records were accepted, compared with zero in the previous run. They are five extracted assays/descriptions from one paper, not five independent confirmations.

D32 refused the first EMSA record: the direction checker encountered antibody-induced impairment in the same passage as stronger minor-allele binding. The repair used the exact whole-sentence selector @span:437:782 at sec3/p4, retained E1017 with direction unspecified and no base assignment, and the coordinator added C5 to H1. The comparison remains explicit in the observed-result text.

C5 is an in-vitro binding claim supported by the named variant's minor-versus-major probes and the C/EBP-alpha antibody result. It is not evidence of endogenous CEBPA occupancy in liver or proof that CEBPA rather than CEBPB/CEBPE mediates the disease chain. Its structured effect_allele field is T, but its text and direction-unspecified evidence do not establish a T-over-G effect; do not count it as allele-direction recovery.

D57 refused an overlong reporter quote. The immediate retry then proposed @span:828:1161, which was not one of the offered whole-sentence selectors, so D63 refused it. This failure was preserved and did not trigger an unbounded retry. Later extraction from the same primary source produced E1018; C10 supports the rs12740374-specific reporter effect in Hep3B cells without a genomic direction.

E1014 is a reporter-design caption without a directional result. E1015 shows dominant-negative C/EBP reducing the haplotype-specific reporter difference; E1016 records C/EBP-alpha addition in mouse NIH 3T3 cells. These were retained as context, not treated as direct allele-comparing evidence for C1 in human liver.

C2, C3 and C4 preserve liver expression associations for SORT1, PSRC1 and CELSR2. These associations do not by themselves assign a causal target or establish lipid mediation. C6 and C7 remain unsupported reporter drafts alongside supported C10, showing that claim reuse/refinement is still imperfect.

The initial QBiC link E113 to group claim C1 was refused because its rationale omitted the member names required by the group-link contract. The final critic flagged the missing prediction link. C1 remains unresolved; no prediction was silently upgraded into an experimental binding result.

The stored outcome is multiple_explanations, with H1/H2/H3 tied. These include different molecular and association scopes and are not three validated competing disease mechanisms. Supported partial claims and unresolved complete chains are reported separately.

The run used 17 model sends, 13 tool calls and 6 literature reads; 357,193 input tokens and $0.082200. The previous run used 18 sends, 15 tools, 5 reads and $0.035150. This change improved evidence retention but did not demonstrate lower cost; decisions, output lengths and caching differ.

tert_c228t.verdict: The new run verified the C228T alias, found a primary promoter study and retained a supported A-versus-G reporter effect in the reported cell-line assays. Endogenous regulation, a specific TF and disease mediation remain unresolved.
tert_c228t.factor_recovery: No supported ETS-member or GABPA binding claim was recovered; the supported finding is reporter activity.
tert_c228t.repair_result: One source-local repair call copied @span:951:1045 from body/p3 after an overlong quote was refused. E264 was accepted, mapped to the case and linked to supported C7.
notes: T4 produced catalogue identity metadata: CIViC variant 248, C228T / -124C>T, was verified as the same substitution through its GRCh37 chr5:1295228 G>A coordinates and T1 NCBI placements. C250T / -146C>T, variant 4004, was verified different at chr5:1295250. Neither catalogue label was counted as experimental evidence.

The verified alias was used in discovery. The early query combined TERT C228T OR -124C>T with assay terms without adequate grouping and returned many irrelevant hits; subsequent queries still reached primary studies. This remains a search-efficiency limitation rather than a successful query-design demonstration.

T11 read Huang et al. (PMID 23348506, PMC4423787; DOI 10.1126/science.1229259). D44 refused the first body/p3 record because the quote exceeded 600 characters. The immediate repair copied an offered exact source sentence and retained E264; the original refusal remains auditable.

The accepted experiment's identity proof used the paper's explicit coordinate definition plus NCBI assembly mapping, rather than inferring a coordinate from the C228T suffix. The paper's C>T notation was converted to genomic G>A for the case chr5:1295113:G>A; the effect allele was normalised from T to A and the original notation/provenance retained. The new catalogue-only experiment-mapping path has synthetic regression coverage but was not the path used by E264.

C7 supports increased reporter activity for case allele A versus G. Its context stays within the reported A375, RPMI-7951, UACC-62, T24 and HepG2 assays; it does not become a generic tissue or endogenous-locus claim. The selected sentence is interpreted with its source paragraph and explicit variant definition, not as a standalone allele-identifying quote.

C7 is retained as an optional molecular finding in H3. Required C3 (endogenous regulatory activity) remains unassessed; the stored whole-hypothesis outcome is no_supported_explanation. This does not erase the supported reporter finding. C6 is an earlier unassessed duplicate draft.

C1/C2 binding hypotheses remain unassessed. Their initial model-sharing-group prediction links were refused because the rationale did not identify a member; no ETS-member-specific or GABPA binding experiment was accepted. Regulatory overlaps C4/C5 remain annotations, not allelic effects.

The run used 17 model sends, 15 tool calls and 7 literature reads; 286,659 input tokens and $0.042341. One literature experiment was accepted, compared with zero previously. There is no complete variant-to-cancer chain, and this single positive development case does not test specificity.
